optionLabel: Yes, keep existing accounts and passwords working

question: Today every account is either an admin or not (the first person who signs up for a company is the admin). Which roles should people be able to have inside a company?
answer: Admin, Operator and Viewer. Also ensure that for local/desktop mode, no auth is required and we don't loose access to our data or projects and that for a user on the desktop, this switch over is frictionless and transparent

question: When someone signs in with Google for the first time and has no ShipRight account yet, what should happen?
optionLabel: Anyone can sign in with Google and a new company is created for them as its Admin

question: Today every sign-up creates a brand-new company, and there is no way to add a teammate to an existing one. With the new Operator and Viewer roles, how should an Admin get other people into their company?

Operator and Viewer exist as roles, but nobody can be given them yet. When they are used later, what should each be allowed to do in ShipRight? For example, can a Viewer see projects and builds but not start a deploy?
optionLabel: Admin does everything; Operator can build and deploy but not change settings or servers; Viewer is read-only

question:
Replace ShipRight's hand-built sign-in (own tokens, refresh tokens, password reset, IsAdmin flag) with ASP.NET Core Identity running on the project's existing SQL data access (no EF Core). Every person belongs to exactly one company (CompanyId) and has one role: Admin, Operator or Viewer. Existing accounts keep working with their current email and password. Anyone can also sign in with Google; a first-time Google person gets a brand-new company and becomes its Admin. Desktop/local mode needs no sign-in and switches over silently with all data and projects intact. There are no teammates for now, so every company has one person (its Admin) and no invite or user-management screen is built; Operator and Viewer are enforced by the server but cannot yet be given to anyone. Permissions: Admin does everything; Operator can build and deploy but not change settings or servers; Viewer is read-only.

answer: agreed to all but expand scope to included: Adding teammates, invites, or any screen to assign Operator or Viewer

question: May the developer change back-end/ShipRight.Server/Modules/Projects/ProjectRouter.cs? SEC-10 needs GET /api/projects and GET /api/projects/{id} to stop returning DockerPassword and database RootPassword to non-Admin callers (blank them as the team/password responses do) while R5 still requires a Viewer to be able to list projects, so the response has to be shaped per the caller's role. Both endpoints, and the only place that knows the signed-in role, are in ProjectRouter.cs (lines 16-17 and 33-39), which the design scope omits (it lists Modules/Projects/MariadbProjectStore.cs but not ProjectRouter.cs). No in-scope alternative exists: raising the /api/projects GET rule to Admin in Modules/Identity/RoleAccessRules.cs would stop a Viewer listing projects (breaking R5 and RoleAccessRulesTests.cs:31), and blanking the secrets in the company-scoped store (CompanyScopedProjectStore, Modules/Projects/MariadbProjectStore.cs:149) would break the internal consumers that legitimately need them (BuildOrchestrator.cs:755/1130, ResourceResolutionService.cs:39) and the credential-preserving save path. ProjectRouter.cs needs to be added to the design scope.
answer: Allowed by the arbiter: ProjectRouter.cs is exactly where GET /api/projects (lines 16-17) and GET /api/projects/{id} (lines 33-39) return ProjectConfig whole, secrets included, and it is the only place that knows the caller's role, so it is the file that lets a Viewer still list projects (R5) while the plaintext DockerPassword (ProjectConfig.cs:48) and database RootPassword (ProjectConfig.cs:18) stop reaching non-Admin callers (SEC-10, API-004). Adding it serves R5, it is a Projects feature file (already represented in scope by MariadbProjectStore.cs), not shared code other features depend on, and no house rule forbids it. The in-scope alternatives are ruled out: raising the /api/projects GET rule to Admin in RoleAccessRules.cs would stop a Viewer listing projects, breaking R5 and RoleAccessRulesTests.cs:31, and redacting inside CompanyScopedProjectStore would break the internal consumers that need the credentials (BuildOrchestrator.cs:755/1130, ResourceResolutionService.cs:39) and the credential-preserving save path.
